generic_sampling_rules.text_identifier: Sample from a per-table pool of formatted identifiers (prefix + zero-padded counter); keep format stable; allow near-variants (case flips, one-character edits) at ~2% of rows; NULL only if the column is nullable and its compact NULL share > 0.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Sample from a name pool; allow duplicates (20-50% duplicate share) and case near-variants; NULL only if the column is nullable and its compact NULL share > 0.
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Sample uniformly from the enumerated value list; allow case near-variants at ~2%; NULL only if the column is nullable and its compact NULL share > 0.
generic_sampling_rules.text_free: Sample from a small pool of realistic strings; allow near-variants and NULL per the column null share.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_range: Sample uniformly within the stated range; include boundary values and one step on each side (only literals inside the declared range are emitted; out-of-range literals are used as query literals only); NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_enum: Sample uniformly from the enumerated integer list; emit only values inside any declared range constraint; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.date_iso: Sample a date in YYYY-MM-DD format within the stated range; include boundary dates and one day on each side keeping the table's date-order rules; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.time_hhmmss: Sample a time in HH:MM:SS format within 00:00:00-23:59:59; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.phone_us: Sample NNN-NNN-NNNN; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.ssn_us: Sample NNN-NN-NNNN; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.email: Sample local.part@domain with domains gmail.com/outlook.com; allow near-variants (@gmail.con, @GMAIL.COM, x @gmail.com) at ~2%; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.zipcode: Sample integer 1000-99999; NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For each nullable column, plant NULLs at the compact database's null rate (a column whose compact null rate is 0 gets no planted NULLs); never replace a planted NULL. A NULL-planting pass must run BEFORE derived-column computation so derived columns see final inputs.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_literals: For each equality/range literal in per_column_exceptions, include the literal, one step below and one step above as query literals; only literals inside the column's declared range are emitted as values.
generic_sampling_rules.tie_ranks: For ORDER/LIMIT columns, ensure at least two rows tie at the listed rank on the listed aggregate.
generic_sampling_rules.unmatched_join_rows: For join columns, include parent rows without children and (where nullable) child rows with NULL foreign key.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_values: Each instance uses a fresh pool per table sized to the instance row count; cap re-use at no more than the compact distinct count so variation stays high.

semantic_rules_and_formulas.condition: ser_start IS NOT NULL AND ser_exit IS NOT NULL

semantic_rules_and_formulas.formula: ser_time = printf('%02d:%02d:%02d', (CAST(substr(ser_exit,1,2) AS INTEGER)*3600 + CAST(substr(ser_exit,4,2) AS INTEGER)*60 + CAST(substr(ser_exit,7,2) AS INTEGER) - CAST(substr(ser_start,1,2) AS INTEGER)*3600 - CAST(substr(ser_start,4,2) AS INTEGER)*60 - CAST(substr(ser_start,7,2) AS INTEGER))/3600, ((CAST(substr(ser_exit,1,2) AS INTEGER)*3600 + CAST(substr(ser_exit,4,2) AS INTEGER)*60 + CAST(substr(ser_exit,7,2) AS INTEGER) - CAST(substr(ser_start,1,2) AS INTEGER)*3600 - CAST(substr(ser_start,4,2) AS INTEGER)*60 - CAST(substr(ser_start,7,2) AS INTEGER))%3600)/60, (CAST(substr(ser_exit,1,2) AS INTEGER)*3600 + CAST(substr(ser_exit,4,2) AS INTEGER)*60 + CAST(substr(ser_exit,7,2) AS INTEGER) - CAST(substr(ser_start,1,2) AS INTEGER)*3600 - CAST(substr(ser_start,4,2) AS INTEGER)*60 - CAST(substr(ser_start,7,2) AS INTEGER))%60)
semantic_rules_and_formulas.condition: ser_start IS NOT NULL AND ser_exit IS NOT NULL

supporting_evidence.events_date_text_type: schema: events."Date sent to company" is TEXT; comparison uses date() cast
supporting_evidence.pk_not_null: callcenterlogs."Complaint ID" and events."Complaint ID" are primary-key components and therefore never NULL in generated rows

uncertainty: ser_time formula requires ser_exit >= ser_start on all rows where both are non-NULL; generated rows with NULL ser_start or ser_exit get NULL ser_time or an unchecked rule (three-valued logic). events.Client_ID is drawn as an independent FK and is not forced to equal callcenterlogs.rand client of the referenced complaint; this is the documented treatment of two independent FKs (add a derivation rule if the intended semantics require equality). Enum pools for callcenterlogs.server and callcenterlogs.type come from the sample only and may be incomplete relative to the compact database. Boundary literals outside a declared range (reviews.Stars 0 and 6, out-of-range client.age literals) are used only as query literals, never emitted as generated values. Compact NULL shares of 0 for nullable columns (e.g. client.age, client.city) yield no planted NULLs; the per-instance 'at least one NULL' rule is relaxed to the compact share for consistency.
